title: PMP vs CAPM: Which Project Management Certification First?
dek: Get the CAPM if you're new and lack the experience the PMP demands; get the PMP once you qualify, because it's the more respected credential — and holding a CAPM waives part of the PMP's requirements.

seo.metaTitle: PMP vs CAPM: Which Certification First?
seo.metaDescription: PMP vs CAPM compared on 2026 cost, experience requirements, and career stage — plus how the CAPM can make your later PMP easier.

sources.label: PMI — Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)

body.richText: The PMP and the CAPM both come from PMI, but they sit at different points in a career. For most people the choice isn't really a choice — your experience level decides it for you.
Short version: don't have the experience the PMP requires? Get the CAPM. Already have it, and want the credential employers ask for by name? Go straight to the PMP.

body.richText: PMI raised PMP exam fees in 2026, so the gap between the two is now wider than older articles suggest. Always confirm the current fee on PMI's site before you pay.

body.text: Why the CAPM is the right first step for beginners

richText: The CAPM requires only a secondary diploma and 23 hours of project management education — no work experience. That makes it accessible to career-changers and students. It also gives you a recognized PMI credential now, while you accumulate the experience the PMP demands. For the full cost picture, see our

body.text: Why the PMP is worth waiting for

richText: The PMP is the credential employers list by name and the one associated with higher pay. But you must meet its experience requirement first: 36 months of project experience with a four-year degree, or 60 months with a secondary diploma, plus 35 contact hours of education. body.richText: Don't claim experience you can't document to rush into the PMP. PMI audits a share of applications and verifies experience. Build the months honestly first — the CAPM keeps you moving in the meantime.

richText: If you have the experience, the PMP is the stronger investment. If you don't, the CAPM gets you a recognized credential now and keeps the PMP within reach. Either way, a certification works best on top of real project experience — see

items.question: Should I get the CAPM or PMP first?
answerRichText: If you don't yet meet the PMP's experience requirement, get the CAPM first. If you do, go straight for the PMP — it carries more weight. Check the experience bar in our

items.question: Is the CAPM worth it if I'll get the PMP later?
items.answerRichText: It can be. The CAPM gives newcomers a recognized PMI credential immediately, and the education hours you complete for it can count toward the PMP later, reducing your future workload.
